correctness.rationale: Arbitrary antiderivative tests in x, y, and z give the three conditional laws. Stationarity of x^2/2, y^2/2, and z^2/2 gives the common quantity \(Q=aE[x^2]=-bE[y^2]=-3cE[z^2]\). For nonzero parameters, vanishing of any one second moment forces the corresponding coordinate to vanish on the invariant support; tangency and bounded completeness then force the entire support to the origin. Thus every non-origin invariant measure has three positive second moments, making the sign condition necessary. When the sign condition holds, four real nonzero equilibria satisfying the displayed square and product relations exist, proving sufficiency. The packaged checker independently verifies the polynomial identities and classical coefficients.

value.rationale: The source treats the sign regime as a necessary ingredient for chaotic rigid-body motion and reports coexistence of strange attractors and limit cycles. The theorem identifies the exact mathematical content of that sign pattern at the stationary-recurrence level: outside it, no non-origin compact invariant probability measure can exist; inside it, nonzero equilibrium atoms already exist. The three conditional laws further provide coordinate-resolved stationary consistency tests, while the canonical second-moment ratio is independent of which compact recurrent component is sampled. This sharpens a qualitative parameter rule into a reusable all-invariant-measures structural statement.
